observations: Photo 0: A disassembled complete engine sitting on paving stones, outdoors, with 'PORSCHE' embossed on the intake manifold cover.
Photo 1: Close-up of the same engine showing 'PORSCHE' text clearly on the plastic engine cover, with visible oil staining and a cut/loose wiring harness.
Photo 2: Another angle of the same engine, showing the opposite side with more connectors and hoses, some disconnected or dangling.
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, or displacement marking is visible in any photo.
Engine appears used, dirty, with oxidized metal and grime on valve covers; no indication of testing or running.
A watermark 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' appears across all photos, likely a seller/shop branding, not a proof of authenticity.

claims.claim: We also deal in all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business claim, not shown or contradicted by any photo of this specific item.

risks.risk: Exact engine model/displacement (e.g. V6 3.2 vs V8 4.8) cannot be determined, which drastically changes price.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code plate, ECU sticker, or stamped block number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the cheapest matching Porsche engine variant as worst case.

risks.risk: No proof the engine runs or has compression; wiring harness appears cut/loose in photo 1 and 2.
risks.proof: Video of the engine running or a compression test result.

risks.risk: Completeness cannot be confirmed; some sensors, hoses, or ancillaries may be missing or swapped.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set including the transmission bell housing and underside.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete, deducting for missing ancillaries.

risks.risk: Mileage or provenance (accident, flood, fire) cannot be verified from outdoor shop photos alone.
risks.proof: Documentation or history report, or clear shot of oil/coolant condition inside.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown history, worst case.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the engine code plate or stamped identification number on the block.
Video of the engine running or being started.
Full set of photos showing the underside, transmission mating surface, and all exposed wiring/sensors.
Any documentation on the engine's origin (which Porsche model, year, mileage).
response.reason: The engine is clearly branded Porsche, but no plate, sticker, or stamped code readable in any photo identifies whether it is a V6 3.2 or a V8 4.8 variant, and these differ enormously in price; without that identifying shot, even a worst-case price cannot be fixed.
